It is national NHS policy to place allied health professionals in GP surgeries.  In our practice we have Pharmacists, Physiotherapists, Mental Health workers and social prescribers funded directly by NHS England. 
 
Pharmacists undertake a minimum of five years training combining study and paid employment including
•	Successful completion of an accredited Master of Pharmacy degree (MPharm) , a full-time course, normally over four years.
•	Successful completion of the foundation training year, in one or more sectors.
•	Successful completion of a registration assessment.
•	Meeting criteria for registration as a pharmacist in Great Britain.
Most pharmacists working in primary care will also have completed post graduate training in independent prescribing , a clinical pharmacy diploma course and a primary care pharmacy education pathway. Our Pharmacy Team have had specific training around prescribing of lipid-lowering medications and follow the Humber and North Yorkshire Lipid Management pathway, which is closely aligned with national guidance. 
 
We have no concerns about the competency of our clinical pharmacy team to initiate cholesterol lowering medications and our patients are no longer offered a GP appointment for initiation of these medications.
